definitions.explanation: The spread of cancer or disease from one part of the body to another. The most common usage in everyday Japanese.
A shift or transfer from one state, position, or condition to another. Used in academic, scientific, and general contexts.

examples.english: The cancer spread to the lungs.

examples.japanese: ⟦{早期|そうき}{発見|はっけん}→早期発見：16127_soukihakken⟧なら{転移|てんい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{防|ふせ}げる→防ぐ：02409_fusegu⟧⟦{可能性|かのうせい}→可能性：04818_kanousei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: If detected early, there is a possibility of preventing metastasis.

examples.english: The peaceful transfer of power is fundamental to democracy.

notes:
{転移|てんい} is a noun that can function as a suru verb ({転移|てんい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- がん⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{転移|てんい} (cancer metastasis)
- ⟦{遠隔|えんかく}→遠隔：14381_enkaku⟧{転移|てんい} (distant metastasis)
- {相|そう}{転移|てんい} (phase transition)
- ⟦{権力|けんりょく}→権力：10020_kenryoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{転移|てんい} (transfer of power)

In medical contexts, {転移|てんい} almost always refers to the spread of cancer. The compound {転移|てんい}がん (metastatic cancer) is also common. In physics, {相|そう}{転移|てんい} (phase transition) is a standard technical term.
